subject.title: Feature: Built-in pace-aware rate limiting for autonomous agents

question: Should OpenClaw add built-in pace-aware quota state and autonomous throttling in core, or keep core to usage visibility/hooks while routing throttling policy into the broader rate-limit, budget, or provider-pool design?
rationale: The feature would add new core config/defaults, provider-specific usage semantics, persistent pace state, status API output, and autonomous execution policy, which repository policy treats as product and compatibility sensitive.

options.title: Visibility-first core seam
options.body: Normalize pace/header-derived usage into status and session_status without changing dispatch behavior by default, leaving throttling as a later explicit policy.

options.title: Opt-in throttling policy
options.body: Add an explicit disabled-by-default pace config with doctor/docs/tests proving fresh-install and upgrade behavior before enforcing any throttling.

options.title: Defer to plugin or canonical rate-limit work
options.body: Keep current provider response hooks and usage windows as the core seam, and route policy to a plugin or the broader rate-limit/provider-pool issues.

recommendation.title: Visibility-first core seam
recommendation.body: Normalize pace/header-derived usage into status and session_status without changing dispatch behavior by default, leaving throttling as a later explicit policy.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest available owner signal from recent history on status, provider usage, session suspension, and agent runtime boundaries.
